_doc: A2.9/A2.9a: diario de Dex (su móvil), capítulo 1 (outside). A3.3c: PIN partido (lámpara, tablón, nido, juntar mitades); buzón, felpudo y DOORIS llegan en A3.3d. Formato y reglas en qa/README.md § Diario. Condiciones con la gramática de `when` de A2.6a: flag, !flag, item:id, !item:id; lista = todas. Se reescribe en A3.3.

goals.text: Find Adrian's door code. It's in two halves, because of course it is.
Check Adrian's mail. Nosy is a job description.
Search the porch for anything Adrian hid.

notes.text: Behind the porch light, once it cooled down: half a note. '73..' The other half 'is with the birds. They never sell.'
Magpie nest, knocked down with a fence plank: the other half, wrapped in foil. '..14'. Kept the plank. Might need it.
Both halves taped together: 7314. 'If you found both halves, you're patient enough. — A.' He hid the code in two pieces. On purpose.
Mailbox: a sealed envelope, 'CONFIDENTIAL — PATIENT ZERO'. Somebody important will want to see this.
Adrian's Ledger was under the doormat. A hardware wallet under a doormat. Bold strategy.

hints: Moths know where the light is. So does whatever's behind it.
Hot bulbs don't burn anyone when they're off.
Use the porch light to switch it off. Then take what's behind it.
The birds know more than they let on.
Something long could reach that nest. Fences are made of long things.
Pull a plank off the fence. Poke the nest.
Two halves. One code. You can count to two.
You're carrying the whole code already. In pieces.
Use one half of the note on the other half.
You have numbers. Doors like numbers.
The keypad. The note. Introduce them.
Use the code note on the keypad.
